about: The one place scales, thresholds and record schemas are defined. engine/RULES.md, the tools and the dashboard build read these; nothing else restates a number. Generic: nothing here is specific to one athlete (athlete parameters live in coach/athlete/profile.json).

feel.pain_scale_note: Stored on a 0 to 10 scale so older numeric answers stay comparable; only the four words are asked.

completion_classes.rest: no session on a planned rest day, or rest taken as the fallback
completion_classes.fallback: the fallback was done (its discipline or minutes)
completion_classes.nominal: within the nominal to upper range, or the nominal when no upper was given
completion_classes.upper: within about 10% of the strong-day bound
completion_classes.over: beyond the strong-day bound by more than 10% in minutes or clearly harder than the prescribed effort
completion_classes.none: nothing recorded on a day with a planned session
completion_classes.unknown: cannot be classified (no plan row, or data missing)

rows[0].data_quality: one sentence: complete, partial or stale, missing
rows[0].call: push | hold | restrain (which call this is, per RULES 13)
rows[0].upper: precise optional upper bound, or empty
rows[0].question: one question, or empty string

expected.discipline: run | bike | swim | strength | walk | rest | test | race
expected.next_morning_legs_min: the lowest legs score (1 to 5) that would count as absorbed, e.g. 3

week_json_day.type: run | bike | swim | strength | walk | race | test | rest
week_json_day.intensity: rest | easy | steady | quality | long | race | test

races_json_cutoffs.limit: overall time limit as text, with its source
races_json_cutoffs.cutoffs: segment|H:MM;segment|H:MM, cumulative from the athlete's start (or the last wave, say which), e.g. swim|1:10;bike|5:30;run|8:30
races_json_cutoffs.cutoffs_src: where the cutoffs come from and their label (Measured from the athlete guide, or Estimated from the series standard)

facts_json: Written by coach/tools/morning_facts.py; its sections are documented at the top of that file.
